Export a track to BigWig format

Source: R/track-export.R
gtrack.export_bigwig.Rd

Exports a track or track expression to a bigWig file.

Usage

gtrack.export_bigwig(track, file, intervals = NULL, iterator = NULL)

Arguments

track

track name or track expression (character string)

file

output file path (typically ending in .bw or .bigwig).

intervals

genomic intervals to export. If NULL (default), the entire genome (.misha$ALLGENOME) is used.

iterator

iterator bin size. If NULL (default), the iterator is determined automatically from the track expression.

Value

NULL (invisible). Called for its side effect of writing a file.

Details

The track expression is evaluated over the intervals as by gextract, one batch of chromosomes at a time, and the values are written to the file as they are extracted, so the whole genome's values are never held in memory. Overlapping intervals are merged first, so each base is written once. NaN values are not written. Values are stored as 32-bit floats, as in every bigWig file.

The file is written by misha itself; no external tool is needed. Runs of bins of equal size (as from a dense track or a numeric iterator) are stored as fixedStep sections, other values as bedGraph sections. The file has zoom levels (summaries at coarser resolutions), which genome browsers and UCSC's bigWigSummary use for zoomed-out views. Chromosomes are written in the order of their names (as the bigWig format requires), and every chromosome of the genome is listed in the file, also those without values.

The file is written under a temporary name in the same directory and renamed to file once it is complete, so an export that fails or is interrupted leaves a file already at file unchanged.

See also

gextract, gtrack.export_bedgraph, gtrack.import, gtrack.info

Examples


gdb.init_examples()

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".bw")
gtrack.export_bigwig("dense_track", f)

# A region, and a track expression in 100 bp bins
gtrack.export_bigwig("dense_track * 2", f,
    intervals = gintervals(1, 0, 1e5), iterator = 100
)

# Read it back
head(gintervals.import_bigwig(f, gintervals(1, 0, 1000)))
#>   chrom start end     value
#> 1  chr1     0 100 0.3377778
#> 2  chr1   100 200 0.3400000
#> 3  chr1   200 300 0.3600000
#> 4  chr1   300 400 0.3200000
#> 5  chr1   400 500 0.2200000
#> 6  chr1   500 600 0.0800000
unlink(f)
